name: Hoshama
overview: Hoshama is a male figure from the tribe of Judah, known primarily as the son of Jehoiachin, also called Jeconiah. His identity is rooted in this direct lineage, which places him within the royal line of Judah. There are no additional notes or distinct attributes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Hoshama means "YHWH has heard," reflecting a theologically significant declaration of God's attentiveness. This proper name is recorded in 1 Chronicles 3:18 and was not given directly by God but carries a meaningful Hebrew expression.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Hoshama is the son of Jehoiachin, also known as Jeconiah. Beyond this paternal relationship, no other family connections are documented in the biblical text provided.
scriptureSignificance: Hoshama's importance lies chiefly in his place within the genealogical record of the tribe of Judah, specifically as a descendant of Jehoiachin. This lineage is significant for tracing the royal heritage that ultimately leads to the Messiah, Jesus Christ, emphasizing God's faithfulness to His covenant promises through David's line. Although little else is noted about Hoshama, his presence in the genealogical record underscores the continuity of God's redemptive plan.
